title: Core concepts
description: Account for memory, communication and recovery.

lessons.title: GPU memory & numerical formats
lessons.description: Account for memory, communication and recovery.
lessons.conceptOverview: Weights are only part of training memory: gradients, optimizer states, master weights, activations and temporary buffers also consume VRAM. A 70B model needs about 140 GB for two-byte weights alone, before runtime overhead. FP32, FP16, BF16 and FP8 trade range and precision; hardware and kernels determine usable support.

lessons.title: Parallelism & communication
lessons.description: Account for memory, communication and recovery.
lessons.conceptOverview: DDP replicates model state and all-reduces gradients. FSDP and ZeRO shard different combinations of parameters, gradients and optimizer state. Tensor parallelism splits operations, pipeline parallelism splits layers, and expert parallelism distributes MoE experts. NCCL provides GPU communication collectives; interconnect bandwidth can dominate multi-node runs.

lessons.title: Efficient and recoverable training
lessons.description: Account for memory, communication and recovery.
lessons.conceptOverview: Gradient accumulation increases effective batch size without retaining every microbatch activation. Gradient checkpointing recomputes activations to save memory. DeepSpeed and Accelerate help orchestrate training, but do not eliminate configuration and profiling work. Durable checkpoints need optimizer, scheduler, data position and random-number state as well as weights.
